newsitem.title: USA: S. Calif. homes sales surge in December - report.
newsitem.headline: S. Calif. homes sales surge in December - report.

text.p: Southern California home sales surged 14 percent in December as prices showed signs of recovery, according to a report on Friday.

A total of 19,202 new and resale homes and condominiums were sold in Los Angeles, Orange, Ventura, San Bernardino, Riverside and San Diego counties in December, up 14.4 percent from 16,785 in November and up 10.3 percent from 17,408 for December a year ago, DataQuick Information Systems said.
A total of 3,438 newly-built homes were sold in the six-county region in December, up 58.9 percent from 2,163 in November and up 20.5 percent from 2,854 for December 1995.
Last month's new home sales count was the highest since December 1990 when 3,735 were sold, DataQuick reported.

"Right now there is significant sales activity is all home categories, from the entry-level market on up through the move-up and prestige markets. That's healthy for the market," Mike Ela, DataQuick president, said in a statement.
The December median sales price for all homes was $164,000, up 1.9 percent from $161,000 for November and up 3.1 percent from $159,000 for December a year ago, DataQuick said.
DataQuick monitors real estate activity nationwide.
